newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook-Fuel oil, diesel see support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook-Fuel oil, diesel see support.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market is expected to be supported this week amid fresh buying demand while middle and light distillates are likely to stay steady to softer, traders said on Monday.
Although fuel oil prices edged slightly lower from a week ago, a total of four cargoes exchanged hands last week. No cargoes were heard traded in the two weeks before that.
The trades sparked hope that the market might be supported in in the near term as traders were speculating a Singapore-based buyer might be out to buy more fuel oil cargoes this week.
The local trader, who bought two cargoes at $101.00 and $100.00 per tonne last week, told Reuters that the company was looking to cover short positions.
The seasonal tight fuel oil supplies in the summer from Kuwait would also boost market sentiment and support the 180-cst grade at above $100 per tonne, traders said.

In the gas oil market, Asian diesel price has hit a near-term floor as some buyers emerged to take advantage of cheap oil but the market remained gloomy, viewing demand as insufficient to absorb abundant stocks.
Traders said sellers were still targetting the Chinese market, despite persistent talk that inventories on the mainland and Hong Kong were high.
They said the cheap cargoes were too good for China to resist. Buyers were targetting to buy as low as $155 per tonne, cost-and-freight southern China, while sellers were at $170.
A Chinese trader has been an active buyer over the past two weeks, buying South Korean and European cargoes.

Traders were now concerned that Indonesia's diesel demand for July and August were limited to three million barrels per month, despite scheduled shutdowns at two refineries, as they were said to have sufficient gas oil stocks.
Indonesia's state oil firm Pertamina was expected to shut down some units in the 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Balikpapan refinery for maintenance from July 10 for 32 days.
The shutdown would also cut Pertamina's output for low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) in July to lower than three million barrels, traders said.

As summer demand from Japan, a main LSWR importer, was likely to emerge soon and supplies from Indonesia were tightening, traders said prices could be supported at above $15.50 per barrel level in the near term.
Light distillate prices were expected to hold steady this week amid a lack of firm direction, traders said.
Indonesia is expected to buy around 500,000 gasoline barrels per month in July and August on the back of refinery
turnarounds.
The weak prompt market kept naphtha prices in contango with July swaps talked at $20.35/$20.55 per barrel and August at $20.55/$20.65 late last week.
But September was talked on par with August as fundamentals were expected to improve by then, when petrochemical plants return from turnarounds.
Naphtha traders said they were preparing for the forward open-specification contract meeting in Tokyo this week.
